bonds.title: Government bonds
bonds.intro: LKR treasury bonds: the dealers' daily quotes, a yield curve fitted to them, and how actively each bond trades.
bonds.curveNote: A Nelson-Siegel curve fitted to the dealers' average quotes, each weighted by how tight its bid-offer spread is. Trades are not used in the fit; they show where business was done.
bonds.fitStats: {n} quotes; fit error {rmse} bp. {trades, plural, =0 {No trades checked yet} one {Checked against # traded bond} other {Checked against # traded bonds}}.
bonds.tradeBias: Trades printed {bias} bp from the curve (median).
bonds.tableNote: Residual: the quoted mid minus the curve, in basis points. Positive means the bond's quoted yield is above the curve. “Wide”: the dealers' bid and offer are more than 50 bp apart, usually an administered quote, so it has little weight in the curve.
bonds.oneWay: one-way quote: not in the fit
bonds.tierHelp: Benchmark: auctioned in the last 120 days and traded on at least 8 of the last 60 days. Active: traded on at least 10 of the last 60 days. Less traded: quoted but traded less often.

bond.label: Series
bond.synthetic: No PDMO release names this bond with an ISIN; it is identified by its maturity and coupon.
bond.historyWindow: Free access shows the last 30 days; {tier} and above show the full history.
bond.zTitle: How unusual is its position today?
bond.zBody: Its distance from the curve, compared with its own last 60 days. 0 is typical; beyond ±2 is rare.
bond.tradesNone: No trades in this bond in the period shown.
bond.scenarioNote: Estimated from the bond's duration and convexity at today's yield; actual prices also depend on the curve's shape and on trading.

zscores.title: Residuals against their own history
zscores.intro: Each bond's distance from the curve, compared with that bond's own previous 60 observations. A z-score of +2 means the residual is two standard deviations above its own recent average. This describes the data; it is not a forecast.
zscores.pairsNote: The residual spread between this bond and each bond of similar maturity (or, for two auctioned bonds, any maturity), against its own history. Choose another bond in the table above.
zscores.pairsNone: No pair with enough common history on this date.

execution.title: Trades against quotes
execution.intro: Where executed trades printed relative to the dealers' quoted mid, as a 20-day median. Positive: trades at higher yields (lower prices) than the quotes.

carry.title: Carry, rolldown and duration
carry.intro: What each bond's yield earns over a stated funding rate, plus rolldown along an unchanged curve, per year and per year of duration. The funding rate is the 12-month treasury bill plus 5 bp; your own funding cost will differ.

methods.title: Methods
methods.intro: Every number on this site comes from one of these models. Each page states the method, its assumptions and its limits, and how it was checked.

about.title: About
about.whatBody: A market-information service for Sri Lankan investors: data from public sources, the methods applied to it, and the limits of both. It offers information, tools and education only.
about.sourcesBody: Share prices, indices and market statistics: Colombo Stock Exchange. Government bond quotes, trades, volumes and auctions: Public Debt Management Office, Ministry of Finance. Data is used only where the source's terms allow it.
about.tiersBody: Most of the site is free. Some analysis will be part of paid tiers (Plus, Pro, Professional) once accounts open. The tier rules are applied on our server: information outside your tier is never sent to your browser.
about.correctionsBody: Sources are stored exactly as published, and every calculation is versioned. When a source corrects a figure, the correction is applied and the earlier value is kept on record.

footer.tagline: Information, tools and education for Sri Lankan investors. Not investment advice.

learn.title: Learn the basics
learn.intro: Plain-language explanations of the terms used on ZinvestIQ.

aspi.name: ASPI (All Share Price Index)
aspi.short: The CSE's broadest index: the combined price of every listed company's shares.
aspi.long: The All Share Price Index adds up the market value of every company listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange and compares it with a base value. When most large companies' share prices rise, the ASPI rises. It measures prices only; the ASPI total return index also counts dividends.

spsl20.name: S&P SL20
spsl20.short: An index of 20 of the CSE's largest and most traded companies.
spsl20.long: Calculated with S&P Dow Jones Indices, the S&P SL20 follows 20 large, frequently traded companies, so it shows how the market's biggest names moved, separately from the many small ones in the ASPI.

turnover.name: Turnover
turnover.short: The rupee value of all shares that changed hands in a session.
turnover.long: Turnover is the total value of the day's trades. High turnover means many investors were active; the site also compares it with the average of the last 20 sessions.

breadth.name: Market breadth
breadth.short: How many shares rose, fell or did not change.
breadth.long: Breadth shows whether a move was shared by most companies or driven by a few. An index can rise while more shares fall than rise, if a few large companies move up.

foreign.name: Foreign purchases and sales
foreign.short: Trades by investors based outside Sri Lanka, as the CSE reports them.
foreign.long: The CSE publishes the value of shares foreign investors purchased and disposed of each day. The difference is their net flow for the day.

pe.name: Price / earnings (P/E)
pe.short: Share price divided by the company's profit per share over the last year.
pe.long: A P/E of 10 means the price equals ten years of the company's current yearly profit. Comparing P/Es only makes sense between similar companies, and profits change over time.

pbv.name: Price / book (P/BV)
pbv.short: Share price compared with the company's net assets per share.
pbv.long: Book value is what the company owns minus what it owes, per share, as shown in its accounts. A P/BV of 1 means the market price equals that accounting value.

dividendYield.name: Dividend yield
dividendYield.short: Dividends paid over the last year as a percentage of the share price.
dividendYield.long: If a share costs Rs 100 and paid Rs 5 in dividends over the last year, its dividend yield is 5%. Past dividends are not a promise of future ones.

marketCap.name: Market capitalisation
marketCap.short: The value of all of a company's shares at today's price.
marketCap.long: Shares in issue multiplied by the share price. It shows a company's size as the market values it today.

range52.name: 52-week range
range52.short: The lowest and highest prices of the past year, and where today's price sits between them.
range52.long: 0% means today's price is at the year's low and 100% at its high. The CSE publishes these prices unadjusted, so a split or bonus issue can distort them.

relative.name: Return against the ASPI
relative.short: A share's price change minus the index's over the same period.
relative.long: Positive means the share's price moved up more, or down less, than the market as a whole over that period; negative means the opposite.

beta.name: Beta
beta.short: How much a share has tended to move when the market moves.
beta.long: A beta of 1 means it has moved roughly in step with the market, above 1 by more, below 1 by less. It is measured on past prices (here as the CSE publishes it) and changes over time.

yield.name: Yield
yield.short: The yearly return built into a bond's price today, if it is kept until it matures.
yield.long: A bond pays fixed coupons and repays its face value at maturity. When its price falls, the same payments are a larger return on the price, so the yield rises: price and yield always move in opposite directions.

bp.name: Basis point (bp)
bp.short: One hundredth of a percentage point: 0.25% is 25 bp.
bp.long: Bond yields move in small steps, so they are measured in basis points. A yield rising from 11.00% to 11.25% has risen by 25 bp.

curve.name: Yield curve
curve.short: Government bond yields lined up by how many years each bond has left.
curve.long: The curve shows what the government pays to borrow for different lengths of time. It usually slopes upward, because lenders expect more for lending longer. We fit a smooth Nelson-Siegel curve through the dealers' quotes each day.

residual.name: Distance from the curve
residual.short: How far a bond's quoted yield sits above (+) or below (−) the fitted curve, in bp.
residual.long: A bond far from the curve is quoted differently from bonds of similar maturity. Reasons include how often it trades, its coupon and recent auctions; it is a description, not a forecast.

zscore.name: Z-score
zscore.short: How unusual today's value is compared with its own recent history.
zscore.long: A z-score of 0 means a typical day; +2 or −2 means a value seen only rarely in the last 60 observations. It says nothing about what happens next.

liquidity.name: Trading activity
liquidity.short: How often and how much a bond trades: benchmark, active or less traded.
liquidity.long: A bond that trades often has firmer prices. Less traded bonds' quotes can sit further from where business would actually be done.

bidOffer.name: Bid and offer
bidOffer.short: The yields dealers quote for purchasing (bid) and for disposing of (offer) a bond.
bidOffer.long: The mid is halfway between them. A wide gap between bid and offer means the quote is less firm.

duration.name: Duration
duration.short: How sensitive a bond's price is to a change in yields.
duration.long: With a duration of 4, a 1 percentage point rise in yield lowers the price by about 4%, and a fall raises it by about 4%. Longer bonds have longer durations.

convexity.name: Convexity
convexity.short: The bend in the price–yield relationship.
convexity.long: Because of convexity, a bond's price rises a little more when yields fall than it drops when yields rise by the same amount. It matters most for large moves and long bonds.

carry.name: Carry
carry.short: What a bond's yield earns above a stated funding rate, per year.
carry.long: Here the funding rate is the 12-month treasury bill plus 5 bp. Your own costs will differ, so carry is a reference point, not a return you would get.

rolldown.name: Rolldown
rolldown.short: The price change from a bond getting shorter along an unchanged curve.
rolldown.long: As time passes a bond's remaining life shortens; on an upward-sloping curve its yield then moves toward the lower yields of shorter bonds, which raises its price, if the curve stays the same.

methodVersion.name: Method version
methodVersion.short: Every calculation has a version number.
methodVersion.long: When we change how something is calculated, the version changes and the earlier version stays on record, so a figure can always be traced to the method that produced it.

feedback.title: Tell us what you think
feedback.intro: ZinvestIQ is new, and what you tell us decides what we build next. Your message goes to the two of us who run the site; it is never shown on the site.

topics.data_error: A number looks wrong or out of date
topics.idea: An idea or a request for a feature

feedback.messageHelp: Between {min} and {max} characters. Please leave out your name, phone number and other personal details: we do not need them.
feedback.privacy: We keep your message and the page it is about. We do not keep your name, e-mail or network address; a scrambled form of the address is kept for seven days only, to stop floods of messages. Ask us and we will delete your message.
feedback.notAdvice: We cannot answer questions about what you personally should do with your money: ZinvestIQ gives information and education only.

thanks.title: Thank you
thanks.ok: Your feedback has been received. We read every message.

thanks.unavailable: Feedback is not switched on yet on this copy of the site, so nothing was stored.
